walkthroughs.body_html:
A megacity has a population of over 10 million.

In 1950 there were only 2; today there are over 30.

Most new megacities are in NEEs and LICs.

Cities grow through two main routes:

1. Rural-urban migration — people seeking jobs and services
2. Natural increase — more births than deaths

Push factors include poverty; pull factors include jobs.

Lagos is in southern Nigeria, West Africa.

It has a population of around 15 million and is growing fast.

It is Africa's 5th largest city and a regional economic hub.

mcqs.q: Why do people move from rural to urban areas in LICs?
options: A combination of push factors (rural poverty, lack of services, agricultural change) and pull factors (perceived jobs, education, healthcare) — though reality often disappoints.
Because cities in poor countries are always better than the countryside.
Plates move because of ocean tides pulling on the crust.
Because the government forces them to move to cities.
